paper-mobility-demand-tgan-wgan-2022.summary: Forecasts demand for free-floating electric kickboard rentals, where the deployment is new and the operating history correspondingly thin. TGAN-Modified-WGAN-GP is proposed to address mode collapse in the generator, another named architectural descendant of the first-party tabular GAN rather than an application of it.

paper-ht-fed-gan-federated-2022.summary: Carries tabular synthesis into federated learning, where no party sees the whole table and the two preprocessing steps CTGAN relies on both assume global statistics. The paper proposes Fed-VB-GMM, a federated variational Bayesian Gaussian mixture that learns the multimodal structure of a continuous column across clients so mode-specific normalization can be applied without centralizing data, plus a federated encoding of categorical columns, and trains the resulting HT-Fed-GAN with a Wasserstein objective and gradient penalty. Its privacy analysis mounts a customized membership inference attack in which the CTGAN package itself is the attack model. HT-Fed-GAN is a named variant built directly on CTGAN: the paper states that the architecture of its GAN follows CTGAN's, adopts CTGAN's conditional vector to encode the selected category during conditional sampling, and reworks CTGAN's mode-specific normalization as the federated component it contributes.

paper-model-updating-causal-information-.summary: This paper proposes a causal Bayesian optimisation (CBO) framework for structural model updating, using a coupled-slab case study to show that incorporating causal structure between parameters reduces the number of optimisation iterations needed to match measured and predicted modal frequencies. To build better priors for the surrogate models, the authors generate synthetic observational data using TGANs, describing a generator built from recurrent neural networks and a discriminator using a softmax neural network classifier trained with Adam. TGAN, the SDV-family tabular GAN synthesizer, is run to generate the synthetic observational data feeding the surrogate model priors.
paper-model-updating-causal-information-.needs: Unclear whether the authors ran the original sdv-dev TGAN package or reimplemented its described architecture themselves; no explicit package/import name is given, only hyperparameters.

paper-synthesizing-privacy-preserving-en.summary: This paper proposes a differentially private framework for synthesizing surrogate entity resolution (ER) datasets by learning the similarity distributions of matching and non-matching entity pairs from a real dataset and sampling fake entities and pairs that preserve those distributions while protecting privacy. It targets the goal that ER matchers trained on the synthetic data perform close to those trained on the real data, and evaluates this on several ER benchmarks. It cites CTGAN among prior GAN-based approaches to relational data synthesis, noting these works can only synthesize a single table, positioning its own transformer-based, multi-artifact approach against them without running CTGAN itself.
paper-synthesizing-privacy-preserving-en.needs: Full text not available; only abstract and citing sentences seen, so it is unclear whether TGAN (or CTGAN, per conflicting sentence-level tags) is discussed further in the related-work section beyond this brief critique.

paper-tabnet-augmentation-apporach-stock.summary: This paper proposes a stock-return prediction pipeline for the Chinese A-share market that combines CTGAN-based data augmentation with a TabNet model to address the scarcity of stock data and the low signal-to-noise ratio of financial time series. The authors generate synthetic tabular data per stock with CTGAN, combine it with real data, and train TabNet (and, in comparisons, LightGBM and SVM) on the enlarged dataset, showing improved profitability metrics (IC, Sharpe ratio) over models without augmentation. CTGAN, with its mode-specific normalization and conditional vector for discrete columns, is run as the synthetic data generator underpinning the whole empirical programme.
paper-tabnet-augmentation-apporach-stock.needs: The paper never names the sdv/ctgan software package or shows an import; it only describes CTGAN's architecture (mode-specific normalization, conditional vector) and reports results using it. Cannot fully rule out a from-scratch reimplementation, though no explicit reimplementation language is used.

paper-improving-supervised-outlier-detec.summary: This paper extends XGBOD (a semi-supervised outlier detection framework) by using unsupervised representation learning combined with generative adversarial networks to augment the extracted outlier representations, improving supervised outlier detection performance on several benchmark datasets. The proposed pipeline trains a GAN on the outlier subset to generate additional synthetic outlier samples that are combined with the original data before an XGBoost classifier is trained. CTGAN, from the SDV family, is run directly using the authors' official implementation with default hyperparameters as the generative model that synthesizes the augmented outlier data underpinning the whole empirical evaluation.
paper-improving-supervised-outlier-detec.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether conditional sampling or mode-specific normalization specifically discussed, only CTGAN's general use for augmentation is described.

paper-when-two-better-than-2021.summary: This paper proposes Duo-GAN, a privacy-preserving synthetic data generation framework for highly imbalanced financial fraud datasets, which uses two separate GAN generators -- one for fraudulent and one for legitimate transactions -- to address class imbalance while preserving data utility for downstream classifier training. The authors implement their generators using the TGAN architecture, explicitly adopting the sdv-dev TGAN implementation from GitHub with parameter settings following the original paper's recommendations, while CTGAN is discussed as related work but not run experimentally. SDV's TGAN component is run directly as the generator underlying the whole empirical programme.
paper-when-two-better-than-2021.needs: CTGAN is discussed at length in related work but never run; only the sdv-dev TGAN implementation is executed, which is why sdv_component lists only tgan.

paper-synthesizing-network-traces-case-2.summary: This conference paper discusses the general use of synthetic data and presents a methodology for synthesizing network traces (PCAP files) for two case studies: an entropy-based network steganalysis technique and a network packet analysis teaching exercise. It surveys related synthetic-data work across domains such as software testing and learning analytics before detailing its own trace-synthesis approach. SDV's original DSAA paper is cited only as a bibliographic example of preserving statistical properties in generated synthetic data, with no SDV code run.
paper-synthesizing-network-traces-case-2.needs: Only abstract and citing sentence available; full text not obtained, so cannot confirm whether SDV software or techniques were actually used beyond this generic citation.

paper-collaborative-framework-similarity.summary: This paper proposes ASPECT, a framework for synthetically scaling relational database benchmarks to a desired size while enforcing target statistical properties, decoupling the scaling step from independently developed property-enforcement tools for flexibility and code reuse. It is evaluated on real relational datasets to show efficient and effective similarity enforcement. The Synthetic Data Vault is cited only in a list of prior scaling/synthesis approaches that follow a fixed-property extraction framework, without being run or engaged further.
paper-collaborative-framework-similarity.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV is discussed further in related work beyond this citation.

paper-morse-code-datasets-machine-2018.summary: This paper presents an algorithm for generating synthetic Morse code classification datasets with tunable difficulty, used to study neural network performance and complexity-reduction methods under varying noise and dataset size. It is a machine-learning-education-focused benchmark dataset paper, unrelated in subject matter to synthetic tabular data generation. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in passing as an example of prior work using synthetic data to augment real-world datasets, with no SDV component used or discussed further.

preprint-fairdiffusevqvae-sampling-time-.summary: This preprint introduces FairDiffuseVQVAE, a two-stage tabular synthesis architecture pairing a vector-quantized autoencoder with a DiffuseVAE-style diffusion refiner that enforces demographic parity at sampling time via classifier-free guidance on the protected attribute, evaluated against fairness-aware and diffusion baselines on Adult, Bank and COMPAS. CTGAN and TVAE are named only as prior GAN-based tabular synthesis baselines whose published numbers are reported from a cited benchmark paper, not run by the authors. SDMetrics, the SDV-family evaluation library, is run directly by the authors to compute the shape (density error) and trend (pair-correlation error) scores that form two of their six core evaluation metrics.
preprint-fairdiffusevqvae-sampling-time-.needs: Two distinct SDV-family uses coexist: CTGAN/TVAE are cited baseline numbers only (citation_only), while SDMetrics is actively run by the authors for their own evaluation (api_user); the entry is keyed to the more load-bearing SDMetrics usage but integration is mixed.

preprint-matformbench-benchmarking-evalu.summary: MatFormBench is a benchmarking ecosystem for evaluating inverse-design and generation algorithms in target-driven materials formulation, using physics-driven synthetic tasks across five difficulty levels and a multi-axis MatFormScore metric. The authors evaluate 39 diverse algorithms spanning surrogate-assisted search, deep generative models, and LLM-based recommendation, reporting per-algorithm rankings across 1170 standardized evaluations. CTGAN is included as one of the GAN-family baselines run and scored (ranked 8th overall), with its conditional sampling and mode-specific normalization design described in the appendix; it is evaluated as one generator among many rather than being the paper's focus.
preprint-matformbench-benchmarking-evalu.needs: No explicit reference to the sdv-dev package or its constructor parameter names; hyperparameter table (latent/hidden dims) suggests the authors reimplemented CTGAN within their own unified generative-model framework rather than calling the SDV library, but this cannot be fully confirmed from the excerpted text.

paper-npgc-educational-copula-2026.summary: Proposes NPGC, a nonparametric Gaussian copula synthesizer that anchors each column to its empirical or differentially privatized marginal and carries dependence only through the copula correlation matrix, and introduces a regeneration stability protocol showing that deep generators drift when retrained on their own output over successive iterations while NPGC does not. The whole empirical program runs on SDV: all four baselines are SDV single-table synthesizers at default hyper-parameters, parametric Gaussian copula, CTGAN, TVAE and Copula-GAN, fidelity is the SDMetrics single-table Quality Report overall score over column shapes and column pair trends, and privacy is its discriminator AUC and DCR share.

preprint-synthetic-tabular-generators-fa.summary: This preprint introduces 'behavioral fidelity' as a third evaluation dimension for synthetic tabular data, alongside statistical fidelity and downstream utility, formalizing a taxonomy of four fraud behavioral patterns (temporal, burst, graph-motif, velocity) and a degradation-ratio metric. It proves row-independent generators are structurally incapable of reproducing cross-entity graph motifs and burst autocorrelation, then benchmarks CTGAN, TVAE, GaussianCopula, and TabularARGN on IEEE-CIS and Amazon fraud datasets, finding all four fail severely on behavioral signals despite reasonable statistical/downstream scores. SDV's CTGAN, TVAE, and GaussianCopula are run directly as three of the four evaluated generators, with SDV-specific behavior (its column-type inference, one-hot encoding scalability limits, and standard configuration) documented as an operational finding.
preprint-synthetic-tabular-generators-fa.needs: Author lists affiliation only as 'Independent Researcher', not a named institution, so affiliation fields are left null/empty per the rules.

paper-tabkde-kernel-density-2026.summary: Returns to classical tools for tabular generation: an ordinal-preserving encoding, a copula transform into the unit cube, and a kernel density estimate with covariance-aware directions and boundary-aware sampling, which needs almost no training, stores the model as a coreset of the original rows, and still matches diffusion-based methods on fidelity and leakage. SDV is the closest comparison and the paper runs three of its synthesizers directly, with the headline scalability claim measured against SDV's GaussianKDECopulaSynthesizer; CTGAN and TVAE also appear as baselines.

preprint-datum-wise-transformer-syntheti.summary: This paper proposes a table-agnostic datum-wise transformer architecture to detect synthetic tabular data under "cross-table shift", i.e., when deployed on table structures unseen during training, and shows it outperforms prior baselines, further improved with domain adaptation. To build its detection benchmark, it reuses synthetic tables generated by a prior study's state-of-the-art tabular generators (TabDDPM, TabSyn, TVAE, and CTGAN) rather than generating new ones itself. CTGAN and TVAE, cited to the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper, appear only as pre-existing sources of the synthetic rows the detector must identify, inherited from that earlier work's dataset.
preprint-datum-wise-transformer-syntheti.needs: Unclear whether reference [16]'s synthetic tables were themselves produced via the sdv-dev CTGAN package or an independent reimplementation; this work only inherits the resulting data.

preprint-synthtexteval-synthetic-text-ge.summary: This paper introduces SynthTextEval, an open-source toolkit for evaluating synthetic text data across utility, fairness, privacy, distributional similarity, and qualitative dimensions, with case studies in healthcare and legal domains. In its related-work comparison, the authors cite Patki et al. (2016), the original Synthetic Data Vault paper, as one of two frameworks (alongside Qian et al. 2023) offering comprehensive evaluation and code packages for synthetic tabular data, noting that neither supports evaluation of synthetic text. SDV is discussed only as prior work positioned against the paper's text-focused toolkit, not run or extended in the study.

preprint-dcr-delusion-measuring-privacy-.summary: This paper empirically evaluates whether Distance to Closest Record (DCR) and similar distance-based proxy metrics reliably indicate privacy risk in synthetic tabular data, comparing them against membership inference attacks (MIAs) across classical and diffusion-based synthetic data generators. Across multiple datasets and setups, the authors show that datasets deemed 'private' by DCR-based tests are often highly vulnerable to MIAs, arguing that distance-based metrics are flawed by design. CTGAN is one of the classical synthetic data generators trained and evaluated as an experimental subject, with its generator-discriminator architecture described and its outputs tested against DCR and MIA privacy metrics.

preprint-survey-deep-tabular-learning-20.summary: This is a survey paper reviewing the evolution of deep learning architectures for tabular data, from early fully connected networks through attention-based models (TabNet, SAINT, TabTransformer, FT-Transformer), graph-based and diffusion-based approaches, and pretrained-language-model adaptations. It discusses generative adversarial approaches to tabular data augmentation and class imbalance as part of its related-work coverage. CTGAN is described in prose as introducing mode-specific normalization and a conditional generator to handle non-Gaussian, multimodal, and imbalanced tabular data, but no experiments are run with it.

preprint-flooddamagecast-building-flood-.summary: This preprint introduces FloodDamageCast, a machine learning framework that predicts residential flood damage at fine spatial resolution during Hurricane Harvey, combining heterogeneous hydrological and built-environment features with a LightGBM classifier trained on an augmented dataset. To address severe class imbalance among damage-severity classes, the authors use the CTGAN synthesizer to generate synthetic minority-class samples, tuning its generator/discriminator learning rates and epochs via grid search and comparing against a non-augmented baseline. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, is run directly as the data augmentation generator underpinning the whole empirical pipeline.

preprint-high-quality-tabular-generation.summary: This preprint proposes PSVAE, a variational-autoencoder-based synthetic tabular data generator that adds a custom loss-balancing algorithm, a post-selection mechanism to filter decoder outputs, and the Mish activation function to improve synthesis quality and reduce runtime versus prior neural generators. It is evaluated against TVAE, OCT-GAN, and CTAB-GAN+ on brain stroke, diabetes, and credit datasets using L1-distance, F1-score, and correlation metrics. TVAE, the VAE-based synthesizer introduced alongside CTGAN by Xu et al. (2019), is run as one of the comparison baselines that PSVAE is benchmarked against.
preprint-high-quality-tabular-generation.needs: Evidence does not name the sdv/ctgan library or import statements when running TVAE as baseline; unclear whether the official ctgan package or an authors' reimplementation was used, despite detailed architectural descriptions of TVAE.

preprint-synthetic-datasets-program-simi.summary: This paper presents HELIX, a framework for generating large synthetic program similarity datasets by slicing and recombining open-source library code into samples with configurable ground truth similarity, along with Blind HELIX for automatically extracting components from library code. The authors evaluate HELIX-generated datasets against a hand-crafted dataset using existing program similarity tools, showing HELIX produces realistic, useful datasets of virtually infinite size. SDV (the Synthetic Data Vault) is cited only in passing as prior work that designed the first generalized generative model for synthetic dataset generation, with no code or method run.

preprint-beyond-statistical-similarity-r.summary: A review and practical guide to evaluation metrics for deep generative models (VAEs, GANs, diffusion models, transformers) applied to engineering design, arguing that classic likelihood-based metrics fail to capture design-specific needs like constraint satisfaction, novelty, and conditioning. The authors curate design-specific metrics and evaluate four DGMs on bicycle frame design and topology generation problems. CTGAN's conditional GAN paper is cited only in a passing reference to prior variations of classification-accuracy-style scores, with no CTGAN model run or engaged with in the text.

preprint-usefulness-synthetic-tabular-ge.summary: This workshop paper benchmarks the practical usefulness of synthetic tabular data across four use cases -- data sharing, data augmentation, class balancing, and data summarization -- comparing several deep generative models (CTGAN, TVAE, normalizing flows, and a pretrained LLM-based generator) and concluding there is insufficient evidence that synthetic tabular data reliably improves ML training. Conditional variants of CTGAN and TVAE (from Xu et al., 2019) are trained and evaluated as two of the core generative models across all experiments, though hyperparameter naming in the reported tables suggests a third-party reimplementation rather than the sdv-dev package itself.
preprint-usefulness-synthetic-tabular-ge.needs: Hyperparameter naming in the appendix tables (e.g., discriminator_opt_betas, encoder_max_clusters, clipping_value) resembles a third-party library such as synthcity rather than sdv-dev's ctgan package naming (embedding_dim, generator_dim, etc.), so it is unclear whether SDV's own CTGAN/TVAE code ran or a reimplementation was used.

preprint-shipgen-diffusion-model-paramet.summary: This paper introduces ShipGen, a tabular denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) that generates parametric ship hull designs while satisfying multiple performance objectives and feasibility constraints, using classifier and performance guidance to steer sampling. The authors benchmark ShipGen's dataset coverage and feasibility rate against interpolation baselines and against CTGAN trained on the same feasible hull dataset, finding CTGAN achieves better coverage but far worse feasibility (0.7% vs 51.1% for the standard DDPM). CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run as one of the comparison generators benchmarked against the proposed diffusion model.

preprint-ptab-pre-trained-language-2022.summary: This paper proposes PTab, a framework that adapts pre-trained language models to tabular data through modality transformation, masked-language fine-tuning, and classification fine-tuning, achieving strong AUC scores on eight tabular classification benchmarks compared to XGBoost and other neural baselines. In discussing prior numerical-based representation-learning methods, the authors note such methods often suffer from a shortage of labeled data, citing the CTGAN paper as one example. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing as related prior work and is neither run nor benchmarked.

preprint-which-best-model-2022.summary: This paper proposes a meta-learning approach to select the optimal classifier and hyperparameter configuration for a given tabular classification dataset, using 62 meta-features and a multilabel classifier trained on a meta-dataset built from real and synthetic problems. To enlarge training data, the authors use two synthetic-data generation strategies, one of which is Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN), employed to produce extra training instances from real-world classification problems. CTGAN, with its mode-specific normalization and conditional generator, is run as one of the two data-generation approaches underpinning the empirical meta-dataset.
preprint-which-best-model-2022.needs: Full text does not explicitly name the sdv-dev package or import statement; it is unclear whether the official CTGAN library was run or a reimplementation was used, though the detailed technical description (mode-specific normalization, conditional generator) matches the original CTGAN paper closely.

preprint-synthetic-generation-economists.summary: A brief overview presented at the AEA Annual Meeting surveying generative modeling approaches economists can use to release synthetic versions of sensitive or proprietary data, enabling reproducibility without disclosing true data. The paper walks through methods including Gaussian-copula-based approaches, differential privacy techniques, and GAN/autoencoder-based generators, describing their strengths and privacy limitations at a conceptual level rather than running experiments. It describes the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) as a comprehensive method that uses a multivariate Gaussian Copula to model covariances and generate synthetic relational data, citing SDV's original proof-of-concept study, but does not run SDV itself.

preprint-when-machine-learning-meets-202.summary: A survey of the intersection of machine learning and privacy, covering private machine learning, ML-aided privacy protection, and ML-based privacy attacks and defenses, with a taxonomy of the current literature and identification of open research directions. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) is cited only in the reference list as prior work on generative adversarial synthesis of tabular data, with no engagement in the body text.

thesis-applications-machine-learning-net.summary: A PhD dissertation applying a Conditional Variational Autoencoder (C-VAE) to network intrusion detection, and using the same generative approach to synthesize predictor features that preserve the original probability distribution, enabling recovery of damaged datasets or those with missing features. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited in this context, apparently as related work on synthetic data generation rather than as a library that was run.
